name: Political instability
value: No G20 collapse; Indonesia VP vote 9 Dec
summary: Indonesia's assembly will pick a new vice-president on 9 Dec under the constitution; no G20 collapse or coup found
state: Indonesia's People's Consultative Assembly is filling the vice-presidency vacated by Gibran Rakabuming through a constitutional vote, first set for 2 Dec (Jakarta Post, 13 Nov) and then moved to 9 Dec over scheduling and verification (Metro TV). Searches on 26 Nov found no G20 government collapse, contested election or coup anywhere in the past month, so the level stays Normal.
for_you: No direct effect for most readers; a constitutional succession in Indonesia is proceeding on schedule.
rubric_hit: No G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in past month = Normal

sources.title: The Jakarta Post — Assembly will pick new vice president to replace Gibran on Dec 2
Metro TV — MPR plenary session to elect vice president moved to December 9

why: Coups, contested elections and constitutional crises in large economies unsettle markets, alliances and policy.
drivers: Elections, government collapses, coups, emergency rule, mass protest movements.

rubric.alert: Coup or constitutional crisis in a G20 country, or deadly unrest threatening a G20 government.
rubric.watch: Government collapse or contested election in a G20 country, or a coup anywhere.
rubric.normal: No G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in the past month.
